questions.why: Maison is feminine singular, so grand takes -e and nothing more. The -e is not silent decoration: it makes the d audible, so grande is something you hear.
An adjective that already ends in -e has no separate feminine form. Un homme jeune, une femme jeune.
An adjective ending in -s or -x does not add another -s in the masculine plural. Same for heureux and vieux.

questions.q: What is the feminine singular of « heureux » ?
questions.why: The -eux ending becomes -euse: paresseux/paresseuse, délicieux/délicieuse. The masculine plural, by contrast, stays heureux.

questions.q: Write the feminine singular of « neuf ».
questions.why: Adjectives in -f switch to -ve: actif/active, vif/vive. Note this is the -f rule, not the fully irregular list.
Beau, nouveau, vieux, fou and mou have a third masculine form before a vowel or mute h: bel, nouvel, vieil, fol, mol. Ami is still masculine, so nouvelle is wrong.
Vieux has the fully irregular feminine vieille. The masculine before a vowel would be vieil, as in un vieil arbre.

questions.q: Build the phrase: a big red house
questions.why: Grand is a BAGS adjective (size), so it comes before the noun; colours always come after. Both agree as feminine singular.

questions.q: In writing, which is correct for « good ideas » ?
questions.why: When a plural adjective stands before the noun, des shortens to de. The adjective still agrees: bonnes, feminine plural. Casual speech often keeps des, but writing does not.

questions.q: What does « un ancien professeur » mean?
questions.why: Before the noun the adjective is figurative, after it literal. Un professeur ancien would be an aged one; un livre ancien is an antique book.

questions.q: Complete so it means « last week »: « la semaine ___ »
questions.why: After the noun, dernier is literal: la semaine dernière is last week. Before it, la dernière semaine means the final week of a series.

questions.q: très or beaucoup? « Elle est ___ intelligente. »
questions.why: Très modifies adjectives and adverbs; beaucoup modifies verbs or attaches to a quantity with de. Beaucoup intelligent is not possible.

questions.q: Which is correct for « I like this film a lot » ?
questions.why: Beaucoup modifies the verb aimer. Très can never modify a verb, and très beaucoup does not exist. The test: if English accepts a lot, use beaucoup.
Bel is the masculine form used before a vowel or mute h, and it links straight onto homme. Un beau homme is not said.

questions.q: What does BAGS stand for, and give one adjective for each letter?
a: Beauty (beau, joli), Age (jeune, vieux, nouveau, ancien), Goodness (bon, mauvais, meilleur, gentil), Size (grand, petit, gros, long, haut) — these go before the noun; everything else, including colours, shapes, nationalities and past participles, goes after.
questions.why: BAGS is the whole of the exception. Anything not on that short list, plus autre, même, tout, chaque, premier and dernier, follows the noun by default.
